title: PolarisX three-way port + runtime parity demo
summary: Intro + parity mapping walkthrough for PolarisX migration from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Demo covered API call parity, console routing, Optimize recommendations (batching, quant, KV cache), and private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed next steps: run small benchmark pilot, share security pack, provide pricing sketch and sample rollout plan.
next_steps: Redwood: send security pack + SOC2/ISO docs (Maya)
Redwood: share pilot test plan and benchmarking script (Alex)
PolarisX: confirm pilot data set and target endpoints (Jordan)
Schedule deep bench run next week (mutually agreed)
Provide preliminary pricing sketch for 6-month pilot (Alex)
action_items: Maya Chen - prepare and send SOC2 + KMS integration notes by 2026-02-24
Alex Rivera - share pilot test harness and cost model spreadsheet by 2026-02-21
Jordan Park - provide sample traffic pattern and 3 representative prompts by 2026-02-21
Sofia Ivanova - list specific compliance controls and approved KMS vendors by 2026-02-23
questions: How do we map TogetherAI streaming hooks to Redwood streaming?
Will Redwood support pinned model versions in Dedicated?
What's the expected token-cost delta switching to 4-bit quantization?
How are audit logs surfaced for Private deployments?
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-02-19 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Tom Bhatia (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (PolarisX Eng Lead), Priya Shah (CTO), Evan Morales (Platform SRE), Sofia Ivanova (Security)

[00:00] Alex Rivera: hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick audio check?
[00:12] Jordan Park: good here, loud and clear.
[00:18] Priya Shah: good, thanks Alex. we got a tight agenda so maybe 45 min.
[00:27] Alex Rivera: yeah 40ish. i'll do a short framing then maya will walk through the parity map and console, then tom will show Optimize suggestions, then q&a and next steps.
[00:40] Maya Chen: hi all, hi polarisx team, excited to run through what a three way port from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together looks like to Redwood. i'll call out common gotchas — streaming, function calling, kv cache semantics, and routing fallbacks.
[00:55] Evan Morales: quick thing, we run a mix of streaming chat for product and batch classification for search. cost is a big driver.
[01:05] Alex Rivera: noted, cost + latency is the core tradeoff. high-level: Redwood exposes the same text/chat/embeddings endpoints, you can use our adapter layer or drop in an SDK change. for streaming we map the chunked responses to the same client events.
[01:26] Maya Chen: starting parity table, share screen (link to deck: https://drive.google.com/polarisx-redwood-parity).
[01:32] [01:32] Maya Chen: first row: OpenAI chat completions -> Redwood chat endpoint. parameters: model, max_tokens, temperature map one-to-one. a small gotcha: OpenAI "stop" behavior sometimes chunked, we emulate but recommend explicit end tokens for exact parity.
[01:52] Jordan Park: ok that's fine, we have a couple hundred prompts that rely on stop sequences. any change to streaming behavior risk?
[02:01] Maya Chen: there can be minor differences in tokenization across open models; we have an option to use byte-level tokenization and we surface token counts in Console so you can sanity check during pilot.
[02:17] Priya Shah: how about Together's multimodal hooks? we use Together streaming for real-time assistant with low latency.
[02:27] Tom Bhatia: Together streaming maps to Redwood streaming, the main change is the client-side event name — we provide shim libs and examples. latency-wise we hit similar P95 on identical hardware; the key is network egress and kv cache locality.
[02:43] Sofia Ivanova: security question: for the private deployment we will need KMS in our VPC and audit logs. how do folks integrate?
[02:52] Maya Chen: we support customer-managed KMS via standard APIs (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault). for Private there is an on-prem agent and logs can be pushed to your SIEM. we'll include the integration guide in the security pack.
[03:09] Alex Rivera: Maya will share SOC2 and the KMS notes as an action item.
[03:14] [03:14] Maya Chen: next section: runtime parity — kernel selection, quantization, and KV cache behavior.
[03:22] Maya Chen: Redwood runtime chooses kernels based on sequence length distribution; so if you have lots of short streaming chats we pick kernels optimized for low latency. we also do continuous batching if throughput allows.
[03:36] Evan Morales: continuous batching concerns me — mixing customer requests could add latency for some requests. can we pin dedicated pools?
[03:44] Alex Rivera: yes, that's Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput. you can pin endpoints to Dedicated for hard SLOs.
[03:51] Jordan Park: what's the tradeoff in cost? going Dedicated vs hosted multi-tenant?
[03:57] Tom Bhatia: hosted is usage-based and usually cheaper at low-to-medium scale. Dedicated requires a commit but gives lower tail latency and consistent throughput. we'll model it in the cost sheet.
[04:10] [04:10] Maya Chen: now console demo: Route policies, per-route cost/latency charts, and automatic fallback. 
[04:19] Maya Chen: (shares console) you can set a policy: Primary = Redwood-fast-7B, Fallback = Redwood-quant-4bit or even a different region. that keeps the app up if capacity saturates.
[04:32] Priya Shah: can fallbacks preserve the same API contract? we need function-calling consistency.
[04:38] Maya Chen: function calling and structured output are preserved; we do best-effort alignment and surface diffs in the Console when outputs diverge.
[04:47] Jordan Park: what about model pinning during rollouts?
[04:50] Tom Bhatia: canary rollouts supported; you can route a small percentage to the new model and auto-fallback if latency or quality regressions detected.
[04:58] [04:58] Tom Bhatia: shift now to Optimize: batching, quantization profiles, and prefix caching.
[05:04] Tom Bhatia: for classification workloads we recommend dynamic batching with a 25ms window; for streaming we keep it low. quantization: we've seen 4-bit quant for many workloads give a 2.5x cost reduction with small quality delta, but depends on prompts.
[05:20] Jordan Park: do you run automated evals? we need to ensure quality doesn't drop on our prompts.
[05:25] Tom Bhatia: yes Optimize ties to your eval sets — you can upload test prompts and our quality regression alerts flag changes per-prompt. we also offer a recommended quant profile per-model.
[05:37] Priya Shah: curious about embedding parity — we have a similarity search pipeline currently tuned to OpenAI embeddings. migrating embeddings could shift vectors magnitude and break thresholds.
[05:47] Maya Chen: great callout. we provide embedding calibration tools and a mapping layer. recommended approach is run AB tests and keep a normalization step in the indexing pipeline. we'll provide a sample notebook.
[05:59] [05:59] Jordan Park: timeline: we want a pilot in 2 weeks and production within 3 months if results look good. realistic?
[06:07] Alex Rivera: yes pilot in 2 weeks is fine — small scope, 1-2 endpoints, defined evals. production in 3 months plausible depending on Dedicated procurement.
[06:17] Evan Morales: network egress/residency: some EU users must stay in EU region for data residency. support?
[06:24] Maya Chen: yes we support regional deployments and private control plane options for EU-only traffic. for sensitive data we'd recommend Private in your VPC.
[06:33] [06:33] Sofia Ivanova: do you have a SOC2-type attestation for the private control plane?
[06:38] Maya Chen: our hosted control plane is SOC2; Private comes with an attestation package and can be deployed behind your identity perimeter. we'll include the package.
[06:46] Jordan Park: switching focus to live demo: can we run a quick parity example?
[06:52] Tom Bhatia: sure — i'll run a sample chat that mirrors one of your production prompts ("product-recommendation-stream").
[07:00] [07:00] Tom Bhatia (demo): hitting OpenAI-style request then show Redwood equivalent. code snippet: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"model":"rw-7b", "messages":[...]}' .
[07:20] Tom Bhatia: streaming chunks come back: delta events with role tokens, same client event loop. note the small difference in punctuation — sometimes tokenizers differ.
[07:35] Jordan Park: that filler punctuation has tripped us before; do you have an escape hatch?
[07:40] Maya Chen: yes recommend a post-process normalization step in the client; Console shows token diffs so you can iterate quickly.
[07:50] [07:50] Tom Bhatia: next, embedding sample: index results for openai-embedding vs redwood-embedding; show recall numbers.
[08:05] Tom Bhatia: we ran a quick local A/B and the NDCG delta was small for your dataset; full benchmark will follow with your prompts.
[08:15] Priya Shah: cost model — can you sketch expected token unit costs for hosted vs quantified 4-bit?
[08:24] Alex Rivera: quick sketch: hosted rw-7b ~ $X/1k tokens, quant-4bit variants ~ 35-40% of that; Dedicated commit pricing will reduce CPU/GPU overhead further — i'll put numbers in the sheet.
[08:38] [08:38] Maya Chen: question from our side — do you have a hard requirement around encrypted logs? some customers want logs to never leave the VPC.
[08:46] Sofia Ivanova: yes, we need logs to be ingested into our Splunk instance in our VPC for the pilot.
[08:52] Maya Chen: that's supported via our log forwarder for Private. hosted can also stream to customer SIEM with a secure forwarder but Private is preferred for strict controls.
[09:04] [09:04] Jordan Park: any pitfalls in function calling? we use structured outputs heavily.
[09:10] Tom Bhatia: function calling translates; we maintain the JSON schema and there are examples in the SDK. some models differ in how they fill missing fields; our Eval suite flags those regressions.
[09:22] Priya Shah: who will lead the pilot on Redwood side?
[09:26] Alex Rivera: i'll be AE lead, Maya will own the security/console onboarding and Tom will run the bench. Lila will cover success criteria post-pilot.
[09:36] [09:36] Jordan Park: great. let's capture success metrics: P95 latency under 250ms for streaming, token cost < 60% of current spend, and embedding recall >= current baseline.
[09:54] Alex Rivera: sounds good — we'll put that in the pilot plan.
[10:00] [10:00] Tom Bhatia: demo wrap: i'll drop links: parity deck, bench harness, and SDK shims in the follow-up. references: https://drive.google.com/polarisx-redwood-parity, https://github.com/redwood-inference/polarisx-harness
[10:18] Jordan Park: quick nit: some of our prompts do multi-step tool calls; will Redwood preserve tool call ordering and state?
[10:26] Maya Chen: yes, we support tool calling and maintain KV cache across calls; we do recommend explicit session IDs to ensure determinism.
[10:36] [10:36] Priya Shah: curious about data retention - we need 30-day logs only, and auto-delete after that.
[10:42] Maya Chen: retention configurable in Private; hosted also supports configurable retention windows per-account.
[10:50] Evan Morales: what does onboarding look like? how long to get a Private test cluster?
[10:56] Alex Rivera: Private test cluster can be provisioned in ~2-3 weeks once procurement and network peering are sorted. Hosted pilot can start in days.
[11:09] [11:09] Jordan Park: procurement is always the blocker. we'll push for hosted pilot while legal sorts Private.
[11:16] Sofia Ivanova: legal will need the security pack and a technical architecture diagram.
[11:22] Alex Rivera: Maya will send the pack; i'll include an architecture diagram.
[11:28] [11:28] Maya Chen: wrapping up now — recap and immediate next steps.
[11:32] Alex Rivera: recap: agreed pilot scope (2 endpoints, streaming + embeddings), success metrics (P95 <250ms, cost <60%, embedding recall >= baseline), action owners assigned.
[11:43] Jordan Park: thanks all — we'll aim to send sample prompts and traffic profile by Friday.
[11:50] Priya Shah: schedule the benchmark run next Tue?
[11:54] Alex Rivera: sounds good, will send calendar invite.
[12:00] [12:00] Maya Chen: i'll upload the SOC2 + KMS notes and include the Private control plane diagram.
[12:07] Alex Rivera: thanks everyone. end of call.

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-attributions and small transcription artifacts (e.g., repeated words, punctuation differences). Shared artifacts: parity deck (drive link), bench harness (github link), sample cost model (sheet link to be sent).
